title: Proximal gradient and accelerated composite optimization

items.title: Extended-real indicator of a set
items.statement: For C⊆R^n define ι_C(x)=0 for x∈C and +∞ for x∉C.

references.title: Neal Parikh and Stephen Boyd, Proximal Algorithms, §2.4.2

items.title: Proper closed convex extended-real functions on $\mathbb R^n$
items.statement: Define a proper closed convex extended-real function g on R^n by nonempty effective domain, convexity, and closed epigraph.

references.title: Neal Parikh and Stephen Boyd, Proximal Algorithms, §1.1

items.title: Descent inequality for a Lipschitz gradient
items.statement: If f is differentiable with L-Lipschitz gradient, f(y)≤f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+L||y−x||_2^2/2.

references.title: Neal Parikh and Stephen Boyd, Proximal Algorithms, §4.2

items.title: Subdifferentials of proper extended-real convex functions
items.statement: For proper convex g and η≥0, define ∂_ηg(x) by g(z)≥g(x)+⟨p,z−x⟩−η for every z; ∂g=∂_0g.

references.title: Mark Schmidt, Nicolas Le Roux, and Francis Bach, Convergence Rates of Inexact Proximal-Gradient Methods for Convex Optimization, §3 and Appendix Lemma 2
Neal Parikh and Stephen Boyd, Proximal Algorithms, §2.3

items.title: Proximal mapping
items.statement: For t>0 define prox_{tg}(v) as the set of global minimizers of g(u)+||u−v||_2^2/(2t) over u∈R^n.

references.title: Neal Parikh and Stephen Boyd, Proximal Algorithms, §1.1

items.title: Strong convexity for an extended-real objective
items.statement: Define μ-strong convexity of an extended-real convex F by the strong Jensen inequality on finite-domain pairs.

references.title: Amir Beck, First-Order Methods in Optimization, SIAM, 2017, Chapter 5

items.title: A proper closed convex function has an affine minorant
items.statement: If g:R^n→(-∞,+∞] is proper, convex, and has closed epigraph, then some a∈R^n and b∈R satisfy g(x)≥⟨a,x⟩+b for all x.

references.title: Neal Parikh and Stephen Boyd, Proximal Algorithms, §1.1
Amir Beck, First-Order Methods in Optimization, SIAM, 2017, Chapter 6

items.title: A finite continuous convex summand preserves proper closed convexity
items.statement: If f:R^n→R is continuous and convex and g is proper closed convex, then f+g is proper closed convex.

references.title: Neal Parikh and Stephen Boyd, Proximal Algorithms, §1.1

items.title: The proximal map of an indicator is Euclidean projection
items.statement: For nonempty closed convex C⊆R^n, the indicator ι_C is proper closed convex and prox_{tι_C} is the Euclidean projection onto C for every t>0.

references.title: Neal Parikh and Stephen Boyd, Proximal Algorithms, §4.2

items.title: Existence, resolvent characterization, and firm nonexpansiveness of the proximal map
items.statement: For every proper closed convex g, t>0, and v, prox_{tg}(v) is a singleton; u=prox_{tg}(v) iff (v−u)/t∈∂g(u); and ||prox_{tg}(v)−prox_{tg}(w)||^2≤⟨prox_{tg}(v)−prox_{tg}(w),v−w⟩.

references.title: Neal Parikh and Stephen Boyd, Proximal Algorithms, §§1.1 and 2.3
Amir Beck, First-Order Methods in Optimization, SIAM, 2017, Chapter 6

items.title: Proximal-gradient mapping and projected-gradient mapping
items.statement: For L>0 define T_L(x)=prox_{g/L}(x−∇f(x)/L) and G_L(x)=L(x−T_L(x)); for g=ι_C this specializes to L(x−P_C(x−∇f(x)/L)).

references.title: Neal Parikh and Stephen Boyd, Proximal Algorithms, §4.2

items.title: The proximal map of the l1 norm is soft thresholding
items.statement: For t,λ>0 and v∈R^n, prox_{tλ||·||_1}(v)_j=S_{tλ}(v_j), where S is the soft-thresholding map.

references.title: Neal Parikh and Stephen Boyd, Proximal Algorithms, §6.5.2

items.title: Three-point inequality for the proximal-gradient model
items.statement: If x+=prox_{g/L}(x−∇f(x)/L), the linearized quadratic model at x exceeds its value at x+ by at least L||x+−z||_2^2/2 for every z.

references.title: Amir Beck and Marc Teboulle, A Fast Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm for Linear Inverse Problems, §2
Neal Parikh and Stephen Boyd, Proximal Algorithms, §4.2

items.title: Proximal-gradient, FISTA, and fixed-period restarted FISTA
items.statement: With f convex C1 and L-smooth, g proper closed convex, and exact prox available, define proximal gradient and the Beck–Teboulle FISTA recurrence; optional fixed-period restart resets momentum after m updates.

references.title: Amir Beck and Marc Teboulle, A Fast Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm for Linear Inverse Problems, §§3–4
Neal Parikh and Stephen Boyd, Proximal Algorithms, §§4.2–4.3

items.title: One-step proximal-gradient estimate
items.statement: For x+=T_L(y) and every comparison point z, F(z)−F(x+)≥L||x+−y||_2^2/2+L⟨y−z,x+−y⟩.

references.title: Amir Beck and Marc Teboulle, A Fast Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm for Linear Inverse Problems, Lemma 2.3

items.title: Projected-gradient fixed points are normal-cone certificates
items.statement: For a convex differentiable objective on a nonempty polyhedron, the projected-gradient mapping vanishes iff −∇f(x) lies in the outward normal cone; a feasible KKT tuple therefore gives a projected-gradient fixed point and global minimum.

references.title: Amir Beck and Marc Teboulle, A Fast Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm for Linear Inverse Problems, Remark 2.1
Boyd and Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, Chapter 5, §§5.1–5.2

items.title: Certified inexact proximal-gradient and FISTA updates
items.statement: Use the exact proximal-gradient and FISTA recurrences with a reported η_k-subgradient certificate for each approximate prox call; an absent certificate returns an inconclusive status.

references.title: Mark Schmidt, Nicolas Le Roux, and Francis Bach, Convergence Rates of Inexact Proximal-Gradient Methods for Convex Optimization, §3 and Appendix Lemma 2

items.title: FISTA energy estimate-sequence recurrence
items.statement: The standard FISTA iterate and its scaled potential satisfy a telescoping energy inequality for every minimizer x*.

references.title: Amir Beck and Marc Teboulle, A Fast Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm for Linear Inverse Problems, Lemma 4.1

items.title: The proximal-gradient method has an O(1/k) objective bound
items.statement: If F=f+g has a minimizer x*, then exact proximal gradient satisfies F(x_k)−F(x*)≤L||x_0−x*||_2^2/(2k) for every k≥1.

references.title: Amir Beck and Marc Teboulle, A Fast Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm for Linear Inverse Problems, Theorem 3.1
Neal Parikh and Stephen Boyd, Proximal Algorithms, §4.2

items.title: One-step estimate for a certified inexact proximal call
items.statement: An η-subgradient-certified proximal-gradient step satisfies the exact one-step estimate with additive error η.

references.title: Mark Schmidt, Nicolas Le Roux, and Francis Bach, Convergence Rates of Inexact Proximal-Gradient Methods for Convex Optimization, Appendix §§6.1–6.2

items.title: FISTA has an O(1/k^2) objective bound
items.statement: For exact FISTA and any minimizer x*, F(x_k)−F(x*)≤2L||x_0−x*||_2^2/(k+1)^2 for k≥1.

references.title: Amir Beck and Marc Teboulle, A Fast Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm for Linear Inverse Problems, Theorem 4.4
Neal Parikh and Stephen Boyd, Proximal Algorithms, §4.3

items.title: FISTA energy recurrence with certified proximal errors
items.statement: The FISTA potential increases by at most (2/L)t_k^2η_k per certified prox call.

references.title: Mark Schmidt, Nicolas Le Roux, and Francis Bach, Convergence Rates of Inexact Proximal-Gradient Methods for Convex Optimization, §3 and Appendix §6.2

items.title: Summable certified prox errors preserve an O(1/k) best-iterate bound
items.statement: If Ση_k<∞, the smallest objective gap among the first k inexact proximal-gradient iterates is at most (L||x_0−x*||_2^2/2+Σ_{j≤k}η_j)/k and the gaps tend to zero.

references.title: Mark Schmidt, Nicolas Le Roux, and Francis Bach, Convergence Rates of Inexact Proximal-Gradient Methods for Convex Optimization, Proposition 1 and Appendix §6.1

items.title: Strong convexity gives linear proximal-gradient and restarted-FISTA rates
items.statement: If F is μ-strongly convex and attained, proximal gradient contracts objective gaps by 1/(1+μ/(4L)); fixed-period restarted FISTA with m=ceil(sqrt(8L/μ)) contracts the gap by at least one half per restart block.

references.title: Mark Schmidt, Nicolas Le Roux, and Francis Bach, Convergence Rates of Inexact Proximal-Gradient Methods for Convex Optimization, Proposition 3 and Appendix §6.3
Amir Beck, First-Order Methods in Optimization, SIAM, 2017, §§10.6–10.7

items.title: Weighted prox-error summability preserves an O(1/k^2) FISTA bound
items.statement: If Σ k^2η_k<∞ under the certified ε-subgradient prox model, then FISTA objective gaps are O(1/k^2) with an explicit constant involving Σ k^2η_k.

references.title: Mark Schmidt, Nicolas Le Roux, and Francis Bach, Convergence Rates of Inexact Proximal-Gradient Methods for Convex Optimization, §3 and Appendix §6.2

title: Proximal gradient and accelerated composite optimization — Examples

items.title: The two-pixel total-variation proximal map
items.statement: For g(u)=λ|u_2−u_1|, the proximal map preserves the mean and soft-thresholds half the difference by tλ.

references.title: Neal Parikh and Stephen Boyd, Proximal Algorithms, §§2.3 and 6.5.2

items.title: FISTA can increase the objective between consecutive iterates
items.statement: A one-dimensional quadratic with a valid non-tight smoothness constant has FISTA iterates whose objective increases from x_4 to x_5.

references.title: Amir Beck and Marc Teboulle, A Fast Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm for Linear Inverse Problems, §4

items.title: One proximal-gradient step for a nonorthogonal Lasso design
items.statement: For a specified nonorthogonal two-column design and penalty, compute the exact first proximal-gradient iterate using the l1 soft-threshold formula.

references.title: Neal Parikh and Stephen Boyd, Proximal Algorithms, §6.5.2

items.title: Projected gradient on the nonnegative orthant
items.statement: A quadratic objective and orthant constraint give a hand-computable projected-gradient fixed point with its normal-cone KKT certificate.

references.title: Neal Parikh and Stephen Boyd, Proximal Algorithms, §4.2
